title: gateway endpoint bindings: unscoped binding listing without endpoint_id is admin-only
answers: Why can a non-admin user not list all gateway endpoint bindings?
Why does bindings/list return 403 when I omit endpoint_id?
How are gateway endpoint binding routes authorized for regular users?
body:
Path: mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py gateway endpoint binding routes (/api/3.0/mlflow/gateway/endpoints/bindings/create and /bindings/list), which handle scorer or other resource bindings to a gateway endpoint.
Rule: A bindings/list request that has endpoint_id is authorized through the endpoint's READ permission; a request with no endpoint_id (an unscoped listing across endpoints) is restricted to administrators, so non-admins get 403 and admins get the listing. Bindings/create authorizes its target through the endpoint's permission and parses modelConfigs/model_configs as protobuf fields.
Symptom: Non-admin users could list gateway endpoint bindings without being scoped to an endpoint they can read.
Constraints: Applies only to the listing without endpoint_id; a scoped listing for an endpoint the user can read remains allowed. The exact validator body was truncated in the diff, so verify the function before relying on its name.
applies: Gateway endpoint binding list and create routes in the auth server.
says: Listing all gateway endpoint bindings returns permission denied for users without administrator privileges.
Regular team members get forbidden errors when viewing endpoint bindings without choosing an endpoint.
Allow users to view gateway endpoint bindings for specific endpoints they have access to.
Non-admin users should not see gateway endpoint bindings across endpoints they cannot read.
Restrict viewing unscoped gateway endpoint bindings to workspace administrators only.
search: Gateway endpoint binding listings on /api/3.0/mlflow/gateway/endpoints/bindings/list require administrator privileges via sender_is_admin when endpoint_id is omitted. When endpoint_id is provided, the listing is authorized through the specific endpoint's READ permission, while non-admins receive a 403 on unscoped requests. Creating bindings via /bindings/create authorizes through endpoint permissions and parses modelConfigs or model_configs as protobuf fields in mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py. This constraint applies only to endpoint binding list and create routes, and does not restrict scoped listings for endpoints a user has permission to read.
